label: Modes of having a perfection and the primitive comparison of modes
term: mode of having a perfection; more perfect mode
definition: `HavingMode` names three ways of having a perfection: `formal` (in the same form, as the effect has it, 'secundum eandem rationem'; cf. IN_ACT_1), `virtual` (in an agent's power, 'in virtute causae agentis'; cf. IN_ACT_2) and `potential` (in a material cause's potency, 'in potentia causae materialis'). The 'cf.' glosses are glosses only: no statement relates the mode labels to the act-frame predicates. The modes are not exclusive: a univocal agent has its effect's perfection both formally and in its power. `ModeAbove m n` is an explicitly primitive parameter: having a perfection in mode m is more perfect than having it in mode n. Distinguishing conditions: it compares modes of having, not bearers in a perfection, and imposes no order law. It falls outside the MORE disambiguation (cdb0de59), whose senses all compare two bearers in a perfection (MoreIn r x y); ModeAbove has no bearer or respect argument. Relation to the eminent comparative of bearers proposed in PR #2166 (MORE_4, EminentComparative := InActVirtually x r ∧ Surpasses r x y): stated independence. No statement relates ModeAbove to Surpasses. The natural open bridge, unregistered, is that for x having r virtually and y having r formally, Surpasses r x y holds exactly when ModeAbove virtual formal; on that ranking reading of Surpasses, granting the strong mode step grants MORE_4 for such pairs. OPEN semantic obligations: what makes one mode more perfect than another (q.4 a.2 gives 'agens, inquantum huiusmodi, est perfectum; materia, inquantum huiusmodi, est imperfecta' for the virtual-over-potential case only); whether a mode above formal possession is a way of really having the perfection intrinsically.
note: Stipulative analyst definition, attribution deferred; the three modes and the virtual-over-potential comparison are navigated from I q.4 a.2 co., first proof (read in the materialized SCTA witness of the I q.4 a.2 passage), and the comparison with formal possession from its 'eminentiori modo'. The comparison relation is a Lean parameter, not a declaration. Introduced for the preexistence assessment (docs/notes/preexistence-bottleneck.md).
